newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan unlocks $500 million aid package to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Japan unlocks $500 million aid package to Russia.

text.p: In a key sign of sharply improving ties, Japan said on Friday it would release a $500 million aid package for Russia which has been frozen since the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union.
In possibly linked gestures, Russia also offered Japan joint development of islands claimed by the two countries off Japan's northernmost island of Hokkaido.
The two pledges were made in meetings between Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and visiting Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Friday.
"We would like to carry out the $500 million in loans from our Export-Import Bank," Japanese foreign ministry officials quoted Ikeda as telling Primakov.
Japan's aid package, originally meant for "humanitarian assistance", was frozen in 1991 following political and economic turmoil as the old Soviet Union collapsed.
The aid at that time was restricted to the medical field and only a tiny fraction of it was disbursed to four small hospital projects before the package was put on hold.
The bulk of the aid package could now be made available for commercial and industrial projects in the form of loans from Japan's Export-Import Bank, the ministry officials said.

Japanese media reports have said possible projects eligible for loans include a car plant outside Moscow, industrial water works at Nahodka in the Russian Far East, and various plants for manufacturing car tyres, baby food and plastic bottles in other parts of Russia.
Japan's latest move on the aid package followed Primakov's fresh attempt to break a deadlock on a thorny territorial dispute which has prevented the two countries from signing a World War Two treaty.
Primakov formally proposed that Japan and Russia jointly develop the islands, called the Southern Kuriles by Russia and the Northern Territories by Japan.
Japan said it would consider details of the proposal that the countries jointly develop rich mineral and fishery resources.
